question: Which structure is responsible for maintaining the amount of water in amoeba?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Contractile vacuole**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An** amoeba**, also known as an **amoeboid**, is a unicellular organism having the capacity to **change its shape**, typically through extending and retracting **pseudopods**.
 
• **Osmoregulation** in protists and unicellular algae is carried out by an organelle known as a **contractile vacuole**, sometimes referred to as a pulsatile or **pulsating vacuole**.
 
• Amoeba has **contractile vacuoles** that aid in osmoregulation by **regulating water balance** and controlling how much water a cell contains.
 
• The contractile vacuole **functions** as a component of a **defence mechanism** that stops the cell from absorbing an excessive amount of water and enables lysing due to an excessive amount of** internal pressure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Having a **digestive role**, the **food vacuole is a membrane-enclosed sac**. **Unicellular protozoans **including **amoebas, plasmodium**, and others contain it.
 
• By **digesting the food that has been consumed, food vacuoles function as an intracellular stomach**. **Digestive enzymes** in it help break down the meal so that it can be used by the body and then **released into the cytoplasm**.
 
• **Cytoplasm** is the name given to the** substance that fills up the cells**. It i**ncludes additional organelles suspended in the cytosol as well as filaments, ions, proteins, and macromolecular structures in the cytosol **of the cell.
 
• **Cells' ability to maintain their turgidity, which allows them to hold their shape**, is one of the fundamental roles played by cytoplasm.
 
• A **flexible, lipid bilayer** called the** plasma membrane encloses and shields the cell's cytoplasm**.
 
• Between the interior organelles of the cell and the external environment, the **plasma membrane serves as a physical barrier**. It is a **selectively permeable membrane, allowing only a limited number of molecules to enter and exit the cell**.
